committees.name: Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee

dimensions.assessment: Involves multiple federal agencies, financial technology companies, blockchain intelligence companies, and financial institutions participating in or studied by the working group.
dimensions.evidence: There is established the Independent Financial Technology Working Group to Combat Terrorism and Illicit Financing

dimensions.assessment: Direct effects are administrative, focusing on research, legislative/regulatory proposals, reports, and a sanctions evasion strategy.
dimensions.evidence: conduct research on terrorist and illicit use of digital assets and other related emerging technologies

dimensions.assessment: Mentions appropriated funds and the return of unobligated funds upon termination, but states no specific dollar amounts.
dimensions.evidence: any unobligated funds appropriated to carry out this section shall be transferred to the Treasury

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a new temporary federal working group and mandates specific executive branch reporting and briefing requirements.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the President... shall submit... a report

dimensions.assessment: The working group sunsets four years after enactment or after wind-up activities conclude, while reporting mandates are one-time or short-term.
dimensions.evidence: The Working Group shall terminate on the later of the date that is 4 years after the date of the enactment of this Act

missing_information: Exact funding amounts or budget appropriations for the working group.
Specific personnel counts for the working group members.
importance_detail.rationale: Establishes a temporary multi-agency working group to study illicit uses of digital assets and emerging technologies, and requires reports and strategies from the Treasury regarding sanctions evasion.
